---
title: "10 — Research results and reproducibility"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** the national out-of-time improvement over a prevalence-only baseline, 2025 AI/AN subgroup differences, and the uncertainty boundaries. It summarizes only results actually computed in the current run. The earlier inspection of 2025 outcomes must be disclosed in any paper or poster.


## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```


## Read final results and state hypotheses

Shows the selected model, temporal validation results, and weighted 2025
population-specific metrics. Interpretation is descriptive unless separate inferential
intervals have been computed.

```{r read-final-results-and-state-hypotheses}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Current-run findings
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load the frozen selection and tables belonging to the attached run.
# Keep the prior inspection of 2025 outcomes explicit when reporting results.

selection <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")
comparison <- data.table::fread(artifact_path("tables", "07_2025_national_models", "csv"))
subgroups <- data.table::fread(artifact_path("tables", "08_2025_subgroup_metrics", "csv"))

cat("RESEARCH QUESTION 1: Can earlier survey years classify FMD in later years?\n")
cat("H1: Physical health and selected social/demographic variables improve\n")
cat("    out-of-time classification over a prevalence-only baseline.\n\n")
cat("RESEARCH QUESTION 2: Does subgroup reliability differ for AI/AN adults?\n")
cat("H2: Observed discrimination and calibration may differ by group.\n\n")
cat("Frozen 2023-selected model:", selection$chosen_family, "\n")
cat("2025 is evaluated as a separate later survey year after model fitting\n")
cat("and calibration are complete.\n\n")

print(comparison)
print(subgroups[family == selection$chosen_family])
```



## Quantify improvement and subgroup differences

**Measures:** the difference between the frozen model and historical prevalence baseline, its relative Brier improvement, and the AI/AN-minus-comparison AUROC point estimate. Optional bootstrap results are displayed *only if they were produced in this same increment*.

```{r quantify-research-findings}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model improvement and subgroup contrasts
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare the frozen selected model with its historical-prevalence reference.
# Read optional diagnostics only when their artifacts exist in this run.

chosen_row <- comparison[family == selection$chosen_family]
baseline_row <- comparison[family == "prevalence_only"]
relative_gain <- (
    baseline_row$brier - chosen_row$brier
) / baseline_row$brier
chosen_groups <- subgroups[family == selection$chosen_family]
auc_difference <- chosen_groups[cohort == primary_groups[1], auc] -
    chosen_groups[cohort == primary_groups[2], auc]

cat(sprintf("2025 selected-model AUROC: %.4f\n", chosen_row$auc))
cat(sprintf("2025 Brier improvement over frozen baseline: %.1f%%\n", 100 * relative_gain))
cat(sprintf("2025 AI/AN minus comparison AUROC: %.4f\n", auc_difference))
cat("The AUROC comparison is exploratory; fixed-model cluster bootstrap is approximate.\n")

interval_file <- artifact_path("tables", "12_psu_bootstrap_auc_intervals", "csv")
if (file.exists(interval_file)) {
    intervals <- data.table::fread(interval_file)
    print(intervals)
}
importance_file <- artifact_path("tables", "13_2023_predictor_importance", "csv")
if (file.exists(importance_file)) {
    cat("Predictor reliance from the 2023 permutation analysis:\n")
    print(data.table::fread(importance_file))
}
```


## Visualize observed versus predicted subgroup rates

Compare the **observed 2025 FMD prevalence** with the frozen model's **mean predicted
probability** for each primary population. This visualization uses the 2025 subgroup
metrics already loaded from the current run; it does not depend on temporary survey
objects from Notebook 08 or rerun any model or survey calculation.

```{r visualize-observed-versus-predicted-subgroup-rates}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2025 observed versus predicted subgroup means
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Reuse the saved 2025 subgroup metrics loaded above. The original version
# referenced prevalence and residuals objects from Notebook 08; those objects
# are not available when this notebook is knitted independently.
chosen_metrics <- subgroups[
    family == selection$chosen_family & cohort %in% primary_groups
]

summary_table <- data.table::copy(
    chosen_metrics[
        ,
        .(cohort, prevalence, mean_prediction)
    ]
)

# A single record per primary population is required for the comparison.
stopifnot(
    nrow(summary_table) == length(primary_groups),
    data.table::uniqueN(summary_table$cohort) == length(primary_groups),
    !anyNA(summary_table),
    all(is.finite(summary_table$prevalence)),
    all(is.finite(summary_table$mean_prediction)),
    all(summary_table$prevalence >= 0 & summary_table$prevalence <= 1),
    all(summary_table$mean_prediction >= 0 & summary_table$mean_prediction <= 1)
)

# Negative values indicate underprediction; positive values indicate
# overprediction. This is calibration-in-the-large, not a full risk calibration.
summary_table[
    ,
    error_pp := 100 * (mean_prediction - prevalence)
]

print(summary_table)

# Display AI/AN alone above the comparison population.
summary_table[
    ,
    cohort := factor(
        cohort,
        levels = rev(primary_groups)
    )
]

# Focus on the observed range rather than a 0–100% axis. The plot is a
# connected-dot comparison, not a bar chart; values retain their true position.
lower_limit <- max(
    0,
    floor(100 * min(summary_table$prevalence, summary_table$mean_prediction) - 1.5) / 100
)
upper_limit <- min(
    1,
    ceiling(100 * max(summary_table$prevalence, summary_table$mean_prediction) + 1.5) / 100
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refined connected-dot visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    summary_table,
    ggplot2::aes(y = cohort)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = mean_prediction,
            xend = prevalence,
            yend = cohort
        ),
        color = atg_palette[["gold"]],
        linewidth = 1.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = prevalence,
            color = "Observed prevalence"
        ),
        size = 4.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = mean_prediction,
            color = "Mean predicted prevalence"
        ),
        size = 4.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = (prevalence + mean_prediction) / 2,
            label = sprintf("%+.2f pp", error_pp)
        ),
        nudge_y = 0.19,
        size = 4,
        color = atg_palette[["rust"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
        values = c(
            "Observed prevalence" = atg_palette[["rust"]],
            "Mean predicted prevalence" = atg_palette[["gold"]]
        )
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.02),
        labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        xlim = c(lower_limit, upper_limit)
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(
            size = 9,
            hjust = 0,
            margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)
        ),
        plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(15, 25, 20, 20)
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "2025 FMD prevalence: observed versus predicted",
        subtitle = paste(
            "Calibration-in-the-large for the frozen national",
            selection$chosen_family,
            "model"
        ),
        x = "Frequent mental distress prevalence",
        y = NULL,
        color = NULL,
        caption = paste(
            "Labels show predicted minus observed prevalence in percentage points (pp).",
            "\nNegative values indicate underprediction.",
            "Survey-design confidence intervals are not shown."
        )
    )

# A Section 10-specific output name avoids the earlier Section 08 figure name
# and the original Section 10 bar chart's existing-output protection.
show_and_save(
    plot,
    "10_2025_observed_vs_predicted_refined",
    10,
    5.5
)
```


## Capture reproducibility details

Records the exact increment, R environment, source-file checksums, selected years, and
assumptions. Keeps artifacts from different runs from being combined silently.

```{r capture-reproducibility-details}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source manifest and session information
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Record checksums for existing inputs and notebook sources, plus the current R session.
# These records support traceability; they do not themselves validate the analysis.

source_files <- c(
    data_historical,
    data_test,
    list.files(file.path(project_root, "R"), pattern = "\\.Rmd$", full.names = TRUE),
    list.files(file.path(project_root, "notebooks"), pattern = "\\.Rmd$", full.names = TRUE)
)
source_files <- source_files[file.exists(source_files)]
manifest <- data.frame(
    file = normalizePath(source_files),
    md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(source_files))
)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(manifest, "10_input_code_checksums")

session_path <- artifact_path("logs", "10_R_session_info", "txt")
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = session_path)
cat("[COMPLETE] Increment", run_context$id, "saved in", run_context$root, "\n")
```
